subject: Re: Renewal negotiation — committed GPUs & throughput runway
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha@helixai.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@helixai.com
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Q4 renewal — throughput needs & ask for committed capacity

Mina,

As we approach our Dec 1 renewal, Procurement asked me to capture Helix's expected inference runway so we can align the committed pool. Quick background: product usage has spiked after the July model launch — conversational agents are averaging 42M tokens/day (peak) and our call shape is skewed to short responses (median tokens/call ~60) but we are seeing more multi-turn sessions which increases per-session token retention.

Forecast request: Can Redwood model our QPS growth for the next 12 months and propose a committed GPU count (and an optional burst buffer) that would meet a 99th-percentile latency SLO of <150ms per token for our current model variant? We need numbers we can use in the procurement pack (commit term, guaranteed throughput, and a fallback/overage rate).

Also attached is last quarter's token histogram and our internal growth assumptions. Would appreciate a quick turn on this — we have an internal renewal meeting on Oct 29.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
VP of ML Engineering
Helix AI

Attachments: helix_q3_token_hist.csv
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Q4 renewal — throughput needs & ask for committed capacity

Aisha — thanks for the data and clear ask. We're happy to model this and propose a committed pool / ramp plan. High level we will: 1) convert your token/day and tokens-per-call into QPS by hour-of-day; 2) estimate effective throughput per GPU for the model variant you're running (we'll preserve your quantization and kv-cache assumptions); 3) propose committed GPUs + recommended burst buffer and a 3-month ramp schedule tied to traffic milestones.

Deliverables: committed pool recommendation (GPU type + count), 95/99 throughput targets, proposed term & discount, and an optional overage rate table. We expect to deliver an initial proposal by Oct 22 — does that work for your Oct 29 internal?

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Manager, Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: none
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-20T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: proposal draft for Helix — capacity & pricing (please review)

Team — pulling together numbers for Helix. Key inputs from their data: current peak tokens/day = 42M, median tokens/call = 60, current 95th QPS observed = 320, daily traffic skewed to 18:00-22:00 PT window (~45% of daily peak). Growth assumptions provided: +35% next 6 months, linear thereafter (conservative).

Preliminary compute assumptions (Ben, please sanity-check):
- Model: rw-open-30B (quantized q4f16) with KV cache enabled, avg sequence length 120 tokens for throughput calc.
- Performance baseline (per H100-80GB): sustained 1.8K tokens/sec (single-stream) -> roughly 30 QPS @ 60 tokens/call; with batching and continuous inference we get effective 120 QPS per GPU at 95th for Helix's call shape. (I pulled conservative numbers from the runtime bench).
- Effective long-tail buffer: recommend adding 25% headroom to committed pool for safety, and a 20% burst capacity available on demand.

Recommendation (initial):
- Current committed: 12 GPUs (Helix's contract)
- Proposed committed for next 12-month term: 18 GPUs H100 equivalent (i.e., +6). That gives guaranteed sustained 2,160 QPS (18 * 120) and with 25% headroom keeps 2,700 QPS effectively covered for normal peaks. Burst pool: add 4 GPUs (on-demand reserved burst) to allow short-term spikes to ~3,180 QPS.

Proposed ramp:
- Month 0 (term start): 14 committed (activate 2 extra on day 1)
- Month 3: 16 committed (traffic triggers)
- Month 6: 18 committed (full commit)
- Pricing: 12-month term, 18 GPU commit at 12% list discount vs on-demand; burst GPUs billed at 30% premium per hour when used; overage rate per GPU-hour if we exceed burst pool.

Ben — can you validate the [120 QPS per GPU] estimate for their model+seq len and flag any changes if we move to an A100 profile or if their median tokens shift? Marissa — I want to include a 30/60/90 day SLA acceptance window and proposed credits if 95th percentile throughput falls below commitments.

Thanks,
Mina

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: proposal draft for Helix — capacity & pricing (performance sanity-check)

All — quick sanity check on Mina's numbers. I re-ran a short microbenchmark with Helix's profile (median call 60 tokens, avg seq len 120, kv-cache warm). Results summary:
- H100-80GB (rw-open-30B q4f16): stable 110-130 QPS per GPU for multi-session continuous workload at 95th pctl when batching is enabled and prefix caching reduces repeated tokens. So 120 QPS is a fair midpoint.
- A100-80GB is ~10-15% lower for the same binary/kernel set; if Helix insists on A100 we should recommend +2 GPUs on top of the committed count to keep parity.
- If their median tokens/call drifts up to 90, effective QPS per GPU drops ~30% (to ~85 QPS). That's the biggest sensitivity.

Operational notes:
- We should include an automatic scaling policy for the burst pool to protect the 99th latency SLO (auto-scale up to burst GPUs for sustained >80% commit utilization for 10m).
- Suggested contract language: 95th-percentile throughput guarantee expressed in QPS, measured per-hour with monthly reconciliation. Credit structure: 5% of monthly commitment per 24h of sustained breach beyond 2 occurrences/month.

I attach a short sheet with per-GPU QPS under different sequence length scenarios (attached to the outgoing proposal). Happy to tweak numbers.

-Ben
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha@helixai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-22T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: 12→18 committed GPUs with staged ramp and throughput guarantees

Aisha — thanks again for the data and patience. Attached is our recommended commitment proposal for Helix's Dec 1 renewal (attachments: helix-q4-commitment-runway_v2.pdf, helix-cost-model-qps-to-gpu.xlsx). Executive summary below.

Executive summary:
- Proposed committed pool: 18 H100-equivalent GPUs (12-month term).
- Staged ramp: 14 → 16 → 18 over months 0/3/6 tied to traffic milestones (details in attachment).
- Guaranteed throughput (committed pool): 2,160 QPS at 95th percentile measured hourly. Effective headroom after autoscale policies: ~25% (target coverage ~2,700 QPS) and burst pool available (+4 GPUs) for short spikes.
- Latency SLO target: <150ms per token at 95th for committed throughput. We will include a 30/60/90 day validation window where we jointly test traffic and reconcile metrics.
- Pricing: 12% discount on the committed pool vs listline on-demand; burst GPUs billed at on-demand +30%. Early termination/adjustment clause: after month 6, Helix can request one-time adjustment (±2 GPUs) with 30 days notice and pro-rated pricing.

Next steps: please confirm you can review this with Procurement by Oct 29. If acceptable, we will prepare contract language and a HubSpot term amendment for signature.

Best regards,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Manager, Renewals
Redwood Inference

Attachments: helix-q4-commitment-runway_v2.pdf; helix-cost-model-qps-to-gpu.xlsx

Hi Mina — thanks for the clear proposal and the modeling. Procurement reviewed the attachment and the ramp looks reasonable. A few quick confirmations before we greenlight:
1) We want the month-6 adjustment to be automatic if our traffic hits the milestone earlier (i.e., if our 14→16 trigger fires in month 1, apply pro-rated committed upgrade immediately).
2) Please include an explicit overage rule: if we exceed burst pool for >12 hours/day for more than 3 days in a month, bill overage at the agreed per-GPU-hour (we're fine with a premium but want clear caps).
3) Can you add a one-time 90-day onboarding credit (to offset ramp instability) — Helix asks for this as a commercial goodwill item.

If you can fold those three bullets into the contract language, Procurement is comfortable moving to signature. We aim to execute by Dec 1 and start the ramp at contract effective date.

Thanks,
Aisha
VP of ML Engineering, Helix AI
